title: Lord, Soothe My Anxious, Troubled Soul
description: Lord, Soothe My Anxious, Troubled Soul in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “He knows your weight of woe,”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, soothe my anx-ious, trou-bled soul, And bid its doubt-ing cease, Speak to the crest-ed waves that roll, To sink in qui-et peace; And bring me to a place of rest, A ha-ven calm and still, Where ev-ery soul by sin dis-tressed, May dwell se-cure from ill.

lines: Lord, soothe my anxious, troubled soul,
And bid its doubting cease,
Speak to the crested waves that roll,
To sink in quiet peace;
And bring me to a place of rest,
A haven calm and still,
Where every soul by sin distressed,
May dwell secure from ill.
Ah! Thou wert once, my Blessed Lord,
By surging waters pressed,
But Thou didst speak th' almighty word
And laidst them still at rest;
And 'gainst Thy soul the wrath of sin
Its tempest fury cast,
But Thou didst stand, serene within,
Till all the storm had passed.
O Christ, the hiding-place of those
Who face the blinding blast,
And battle with a myriad woes
That sweep in fury past;
Be Thou my comfort and defence,
While storm fiends wildly cry, —
My star of hope when night is dense,
And dangers round me lie.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
